Instalación
------------

Las instrucciones completas de instalación están contenidas en 
el archivo de ayuda.
Para comenzar, descomprima todo el archivo ZIP que recivió dentro 
de un directorio que ha de nombrar  Calmira en su disco duro, y 
ejecute el archivo de ayuda CALMIRA.HLP desde le Administrador de 
archivos o con Ejecutar.


Calmira es una interface de usuario estilo Windows 95 para Windows 3.1.
Es un entorno completamente integrado para administrar sus archivos y programas,
y está diseñada para ejecutarse excelentemente en computadoras 386 y 486.

Calmira inculle:

o  Un explorador con iconos para manejar sus archivos en ventanas flotantes
o  Soporte para descripciones 4DOS en reemplazo de nombres de archivo largos
o  Accesos directos de escritorio y archivo para cualquier objeto o URL
o  Árbol del Explorer que le permite navegar rapidamente por sus discos
o  Barra de tareas con un Menú de Inicio, configurable en cualquier nivel
o  Papelera de reciclaje para almacenar archivos y carpetas borradas
o  Cientos de opciones y configuraciones facilmente accesibles
o  Manual de 94 páginas conteniendo toda la ayuda que requiere

La Versión 2.3 contiene una barra de tareas mejorada, un administrador de tareas
propio y operaciones de cortar-y-pegar, junto con muchisimas adiciones.

Luego de que la ponga a funcionar y sienta como se ve y se comorta su Windows 3.1,
Ud. nunca querrá regresarse...


Requerimientos del Sistema
-------------------

o  Procesador 386 o superior
o  Microsoft Windows 3.1 o Windows para Trabajo en Grupos 3.11
o  Mínimo 4 megabytes (MB) de memoria, 8MB recomendado
o  Monitor VGA o mejor
o  Un mouse (ratón)

============================================================================
                 Last minute notes (in English, sorry!)
============================================================================


Tip color -- you can change this by setting HintColor in the [Calmira]
section.  The default is the hexadecimal number $00F0FBFF.

Desktop activation -- in previous versions, all Calmira windows are
brought forward if you do a left+right click on the desktop.  Now, if
the "Treat Calmira windows as separate tasks" checkbox is turned on
in the Desktop Properties dialog, then only shortcut icons are exposed.
You can now also double click on the taskbar panel to activate the desktop.

Bitmaps -- some of the graphics have been updated.  They are stored
in the RES files with the source, but I can send you copies of the
bitmaps by email if you don't have a suitable extraction tool.

Volume labels -- if your volume label has more than 8 characters and
does not contain a dot ".", Calmira will not display it correctly.
For example, "ABCDEFGH_123" could be shown as "ABCDEFGH._12".

Windows 95 colours -- when you first run Calmira, it installs a new
colour scheme called "Windows 95 Standard" into your Control Panel.
You can choose this scheme in the usual way.

Restricting access to settings -- if you use Calmira in a school or
other multi-user environment, you can now prevent the options,
shortcuts, and Start Menu from being changed.  In the [Calmira]
section of CALMIRA.INI, add CanEditingSettings=0.  This causes the
OK button and tab pages to be disabled in property sheets, and
does not allow shortcuts to be created, edited or removed.

Alt+Tab side effects -- all grid and tree components used by Calmira
are affected by task switching with Alt+Tab.  The focus moves to the
next item along, which causes the Explorer tree to change directory.

Switching between Explorer tree and file pane -- press Alt+W.

Toggling selections with the keyboard -- press the Spacebar.

Changes since 2.3 -- mainly minor bug fixes 
(all fixes by Ramon Valbuena)

     Explorer (tree.pas, explorer.dpr)
     * Explorer can be opened to specified directory from command line 
       "explorer c:\dos" willl launch explorer in C:\DOS directory
     * Changed bitmaps to more Win95-style
     * Now draws focus rectangle around name of selected folder
     
     Computer Window
     * Enabled drag and drop to drive icons for file copy/move from Icon 
     Windows, Bin, and Find Dialog
     * Drag & drop creation of aliases for Computer window items
     * "Status panel" along Computer window's lower edge                   
     
     General
     * Functional (if crude) word-wrapped TCheckList component
     
     Drive Properties
     * Drive labels - '.' is now properly stripped out
     
     TaskBar Properties
     * Exclusion and Applet list items can be dragged to change sort order
     * Can modify existing entries via "Modify Button" or double-click on 
     item

Hiding the Computer and Bin icons -- assign empty captions to these
objects, and they will not appear the next time you run Calmira.
The trick of giving negative icon positions does not seem to work
any more.

Source code changes -- there is a summary in the help file, but it
might be incomplete due to last minute fixes.  Do a grep on { 2.3 }
or Ramon Valbuena or { mzo } to make sure.

Thanks for using Spanish Calmira.
